title: BJP Wins 77 Tripura Civic Seats Unopposed as Opposition Alleges Intimidation
excerpt: The State Election Commission declared 77 BJP candidates elected unopposed after the withdrawal of nominations closed, leaving 268 of the state's 345 urban local body seats to be contested on November 27.
body:
• The BJP has been declared elected unopposed in 77 of Tripura's 345 urban local body seats: all 65 seats in five municipal bodies where no opposition party fielded a candidate, plus 12 seats in three other bodies.
  • Polling on November 27 will cover the remaining 268 seats across 16 civic bodies, including the 51-seat Agartala Municipal Corporation; counting is scheduled for December 2.
  • A total of 6,29,903 voters — 3,21,743 women, 3,08,115 men and 45 third-gender voters — are eligible to vote in the November 27 elections, the State Election Commission said.
  • The CPI(M) and Congress allege their candidates and proposers were threatened and attacked to keep them out of the race; CPI(M) leader Jitendra Chaudhury says more than 20 of his party's leaders and members were injured.

The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party has secured 77 seats without a contest ahead of Tripura's November 27 urban local body elections. The Tripura State Election Commission (SEC) declared the party's candidates elected unopposed after the withdrawal of nominations ended on Tuesday afternoon, a senior SEC official said, according to IANS. The declarations mean more than a fifth of the state's 345 civic seats have been settled before a single vote is cast.

How the 77 seats break down

The BJP secured all 65 seats across five municipal bodies where no opposition or other political party had fielded candidates: Kamalpur in Dhalai district, Santir Bazar in South Tripura, and Ranir Bazar, Jirania and Mohanpur in West Tripura district. The party won another 12 seats without a contest in three other municipal bodies — Ambassa in Dhalai district, Teliamura in Khowai district and Bishalgarh in Sepahijala district.

Opposition alleges intimidation

Opposition leaders have questioned how so many seats came to have no challenger. CPI(M) Tripura state secretary and Leader of the Opposition Jitendra Chaudhury alleged that opposition candidates were threatened by ruling party supporters and that their proposers were also intimidated to prevent them from contesting in the five municipal bodies. He alleged that a series of violent attacks across several districts left more than 20 CPI(M) leaders and members injured, and that despite repeated written complaints, neither the police nor the SEC took adequate steps to prevent the attacks or act against those responsible. He further alleged that the state police had failed to comply with a Tripura High Court order directing security for opposition candidates.

Congress Working Committee member Sudip Roy Barman and Tripura Pradesh Congress Committee president Asish Kumar Saha raised similar allegations, accusing the ruling party of using intimidation and violence to undermine the electoral process. The IANS report carried no response from the BJP to the allegations.

The contest still to come

Polling will now be held for the remaining 268 seats across 16 of the state's 21 urban local bodies, spread over all eight districts. The Agartala Municipal Corporation, the state's largest civic body, accounts for 51 of the 345 seats. Of the total seats, 162 are reserved for women, 80 for Scheduled Caste candidates and nine for Scheduled Tribe candidates. The CPI(M) and Congress had earlier explored contesting the elections jointly, but several rounds of talks failed to produce an electoral understanding. The terms of all 21 urban local bodies, including the Agartala Municipal Corporation, expire on December 9.
